## 15. Repository and pins design

**Layout.** The repository is `ChristopherLinnett/craftbridge` (MIT OR Apache-2.0; private until hosted CI starts, then public, PD3), checked out at `artcraft-plugin-port/` (PD16). It has one folder per platform, each a complete build, and nothing of a platform at its root (PD19). Inside each platform folder the universal core sits beside the app plugin (PD10), and samples sit beside the library they consume (D-1).

**Dependency direction.** Within the core and within a plugin, dependencies point down the layers. `rust/xtask/src/layers.rs` lists each crate's layer once, and the gate fails on any edge the table does not allow (D-25).

| Layer | Crate | May depend on |
|---|---|---|
| core 0 | `craftbridge-media` | external crates; `filmcraft-codecs` and `filmcraft-isobmff` at EffectCraft's FilmCraft revision (PD18) |
| core 1 | `craftbridge-core` | a lower core rank |
| core 2 | `craftbridge-core-ffi` | the lower core ranks; `uniffi` |
| app 0 | `craftbridge-effects` | any core crate; `effectcraft-*` |
| app 1 | `craftbridge-effects-ffi` | a lower rank of its app, and any core crate; `uniffi` |
| tool | `craftbridge-effects-codegen`, `craftbridge-effects-conformance`, `uniffi-bindgen`, `xtask` | anything; nothing depends on a tool |

- A core crate never depends on an `effectcraft-*` crate or on an app crate, not even in its tests (PD9). An app crate never depends on another app's crates, not even in its tests: code two plugins need moves into the core (PD18). The rank, `uniffi` and tool rules are about what ships, so dev-dependencies, which only a crate's own tests compile, are outside them.
- `uniffi` appears only in `-ffi` crates, and only an app's `-ffi` crate builds a `staticlib` or `cdylib`, and it builds both; no crate is a Rust `dylib` (D-4).
- Every crate is a workspace member in the folder its row gives it (`core/<name>`, `<app>/<name>`, or `<name>` for a tool that is no app's), its library named after it; a dependency by a path outside the workspace, or on a workspace crate's name from anywhere else, is refused.
- Swift: `CraftBridgeFFI` ← `CraftBridge` ← `CraftBridgeEffects`. Kotlin: `:effects` exposes `:core`. Swift and Kotlin take the same rule as Rust: a plugin target or plugin module depends only on the core (in Swift, the core's targets `CraftBridge`, the generated `CraftBridgeFFI` and its binary target), `CraftBridge` and `:core` depend on no plugin, and no plugin depends on another; the package manifest, read by `swift package dump-package`, and Gradle's own project graph, declared and resolved, enforce this. A platform folder never refers to another platform's code; every platform reads `conformance/`.
- Code and data a generator in this repository writes live only in `generated` or `Generated` directories, carry an `@generated` header where the format has comments (Markdown's being `<!-- … -->`), are committed, and are written only by `cargo xtask generate` (D-26, L10). Three kinds of written-for-you file are outside that rule: what a build tool writes for itself (`Cargo.lock`, `Package.resolved`, the Gradle wrapper), which change only through that tool; the `[patch.crates-io]` and `[profile.release]` tables of `rust/Cargo.toml` and the starting `Cargo.lock`, which only `tools/update-upstream.sh` writes from the pinned EffectCraft (Pins, below); and the plan's views in `plan/`, which the plan kit builds from this file and `plan/diagrams/src/` and `plan/plan check --final` checks.

**Pins.** `[workspace.dependencies]` names each EffectCraft crate CraftBridge uses (`effectcraft-engine`, `-host`, `-automation`, `-gpu`, `-render`, `-time`, `-text`, `-media`, `-expr`, `-script`, `-plugin`) with `git = "https://github.com/storytold/effectcraft"` and one `rev`, an official revision (`10376058` at the start, PD4, PD17), and `filmcraft-codecs` and `filmcraft-isobmff` with EffectCraft's own FilmCraft revision `d5ead4ba` (`effectcraft: Cargo.toml:89-90`), so CraftBridge's decoders register into the same registry EffectCraft decodes through (D-13).

- Cargo applies `[patch]` tables only at the root workspace, so EffectCraft's own `[patch.crates-io]` entries (`hayro-syntax`, `hayro-jbig2` and the egui family, `effectcraft: Cargo.toml:223-239`) and its `[profile.release]` (`effectcraft: Cargo.toml:219-221`) are **generated** into `rust/Cargo.toml` from the pinned upstream `Cargo.toml` by `tools/update-upstream.sh`, and `Cargo.lock` starts from the pinned upstream `Cargo.lock`. No line of them is written by hand (D-21).
- Nothing in EffectCraft is changed, and CraftBridge never builds from a fork or a patched branch; the fork `ChristopherLinnett/effectcraft` is only kept in step with upstream (PD17).

**The adaptations** (PD5, D-29). Where a phone needs EffectCraft to do something differently, CraftBridge does it in its own crates on EffectCraft's public interfaces, never by copying EffectCraft code. `tools/adaptations.toml` lists each adaptation with the EffectCraft files and items it relies on, so the update script names the adaptations an update touches (§24).

| ID | Adaptation in CraftBridge | Instead of | Relies on (EffectCraft at `10376058`) | Task |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AD1 | `craftbridge-effects` builds its own `Session` from the public fields: models and plug-ins folders from the app's `Folders`, EffectCraft's `MediaPool`, an importer over `effectcraft_media::probe`, CraftBridge's exporter (AD7), `effectcraft_expr`'s expressions and syntax check, the plug-in loader of PD13 and no helper hooks; then `effectcraft_script::install` | `effectcraft_host::session()`, which takes its folders from `EFFECTCRAFT_CONFIG_DIR` or the desktop conventions and starts external helpers (`effectcraft: crates/host/src/lib.rs:96-147`; `evidence/03-device-feasibility.md` Finding 11; `evidence/05-mobile-platforms.md` Findings 14–15) | `Session` (`effectcraft: crates/engine/src/lib.rs:104-269`), `effectcraft_media::probe` (`effectcraft: crates/media/src/probe.rs:17`), `effectcraft_script::install` (`effectcraft: crates/script/src/lib.rs:78`) | FX-1a |
| AD2 | At engine start, `effectcraft_text::fonts::add_source(&DirectorySource { dirs })` with the phone's font folders and `Folders.fonts`: on iOS the parent folders of the font files CoreText reports (`CTFontCollectionCreateFromAvailableFonts`, `kCTFontURLAttribute`), never a hard-coded `/System/Library/Fonts`, which in the simulator is the Mac's and on a phone misses PingFang's `CorePrivate` (V1); on Android `/system/fonts`. Every face stays registered for drawing and fallback; `craftbridge-effects` filters the font list on every app-facing call (the `list_fonts` method, `exec` of `text.fonts`, the MCP tools that reach it) to the faces CoreText offers, matched by (file, PostScript name), plus the bundled ones, passing it through where no face list is supplied; code inside EffectCraft's own dispatch (scripts, `engine.batch`) sees the full registry | `DirectorySource::system()`, which knows the macOS, Windows and Unix desktop folders (`effectcraft: crates/text/src/fonts.rs:79-101`; `evidence/03-device-feasibility.md` Finding 10) | `FontSource`, `DirectorySource` (`effectcraft: crates/text/src/fonts.rs:67-76`), `add_source` (`:396-412`), `add_font_data` (`:414-422`), `text.fonts` (`effectcraft: crates/engine/src/cmd/text_edit.rs:880-903`), `effectcraft_text::families` | FX-3 |
| AD3 | `RenderRequest` (one field per `render` flag, mapped to the render-queue parameters with the CLI's names, defaults and errors) and the render runner: unqueue the project's other items, add this one, render without waiting, poll every 100 ms, report progress, stop on cancel, report failed items | the CLI's flag handling and queue-and-wait loop, which live in its binary (`effectcraft: apps/effectcraft-cli/src/main.rs:860-1037`) | the `renderQueue.add` and `renderQueue.render` commands; `render_progress`, `stop_render` and `poll_render` (`effectcraft: crates/engine/src/render_queue.rs:545`, `:692`, `:723`) | FX-1c |
| AD4 | `FrameRequest`: comp, time or frame, maximum side or scale, transparency, resolved as `render-frame` resolves them | the CLI's `render-frame` (`effectcraft: apps/effectcraft-cli/src/main.rs:789-821`) | `Session::render_rgba8_alpha` (`effectcraft: crates/engine/src/session/render.rs:132-143`), `Backend::render_with` (`effectcraft: crates/automation/src/backend.rs:122-124`) | FX-1e |
| AD5 | Templates: open an `.ectemplate`, apply values, render a frame or an export, and surface missing-font warnings | the CLI's `--template` (`effectcraft: apps/effectcraft-cli/src/template.rs`) | the `essential` and `templates` commands | FX-1f |
| AD6 | Render timings per layer and effect, CPU against GPU, in the shape of the CLI's `bench` | the CLI's `bench` (`effectcraft: apps/effectcraft-cli/src/main.rs:1265-1350`, `:1507-1616`) | `effectcraft_render::Renderer`, `LayerCache`, `LayerTiming` (`effectcraft: crates/render/src/lib.rs:66`, `effectcraft: crates/render/src/opts.rs:92`) | FX-1d |
| AD7 | CraftBridge's exporter, set as `Session.exporter`: it hands each job to EffectCraft's `FileExporter` inside a thread pool with as many threads as half the memory the phone reports available holds output frames at 16 bytes a pixel, between one and the core count; from W6 it also encodes H.264 and HEVC in hardware (§18) | `FileExporter` alone, whose free-memory figure is empty on iOS and Android because `sysinfo::memory()` has no branch for either (`effectcraft: crates/host/src/lib.rs:91-94`, `effectcraft: crates/engine/src/system/sysinfo.rs:142-168`), which leaves frames in flight bounded only by the thread count (`effectcraft: crates/export/src/pipeline.rs:140-149`, `:171-176`) | `Exporter`, `ExportJob` (`effectcraft: crates/engine/src/render_queue.rs:93-113`, `:22-46`), `FileExporter` (`effectcraft: crates/host/src/lib.rs:25-89`), the export frame loop's thread count | FX-1g, MED-3 |

**States.**
- *Pinned*: `rev` is an official storytold/effectcraft commit; `info` reports it as `pin`.
- *Update in progress*: the update script has moved the pin and named the adaptations whose EffectCraft code changed; the update merges once each named adaptation is rechecked and the gate passes (§24).

**Edge cases.**
- An update changes code an adaptation follows (a new `render` flag, a renamed command an adaptation calls): the script names the adaptation; `RenderRequest` gains the field and the corpus the scenario, in the same update.
- An update removes a public item an adaptation uses: the build fails at the gate, and the adaptation is rewritten on what upstream offers instead, in the same update.
- Upstream adds a public interface that does what an adaptation does (a session with explicit folders, an encoder interface): the adaptation moves onto it and leaves `tools/adaptations.toml` (upstream wins).

**The gate.** `tools/ci.sh` is the one entry point for people, agents and CI (D-25). It runs `tools/doctor.sh --gate`, then every stage, and one run reports every failure; `tools/ci.sh <stage or group>…` runs only those named, every name checked before the first runs.

| Stage | Checks |
|---|---|
| Rust | `cargo fmt --check`; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -D warnings`; `cargo test --workspace`; `cargo clippy -D warnings` of the libraries for each of the four mobile targets, so the platform modules, which only the phones compile, meet the never-crash lints and carry their `// SAFETY:` comments; `cargo deny check licenses bans sources` over every feature; no cargo stage runs while the repository root holds a `.cargo` folder |
| Rules | `cargo xtask rules`: the root and platform-folder layout, with no `node_modules` in the code folders; layers and dependency direction, in Swift too (the manifest, read by `swift package dump-package`), with no plugin depending on a plugin; the inherited lint table, its five no-exception lints `forbid`, weakened by no crate, module, item (bar `expect_used`'s literal), clippy configuration, Cargo configuration, target runner or compiler wrapper, with a build script (as `cargo metadata` reports it) only for a crate the layer table marks, no `#[path]` or `include!`, and `panic = "unwind"`; `unsafe` only in platform modules (D-20), read from Rust's syntax tree by `syn` (D-28); generated-file placement; one copy of each gate configuration, and none of the tool configurations that would switch a check off (Gate machinery, below); the licences of what the builds ship — every external module resolved onto a Gradle library module's release runtime classpath, every package a `Package.swift` names (as `swift package dump-package` reads it) and every pin a `Package.resolved` records, each declared in `tools/licences.toml`, with build plugins checked by name from the catalog's `[plugins]`; one copy of each EffectCraft, FilmCraft and Craft library crate (D-13) |
| Generated | `cargo xtask generate --check`: everything regenerated, any difference fails, and so does a file there git does not track (L10) |
| Swift | `swift format lint --strict` on every Swift file, symbolic links followed, whose never-crash rules (force unwraps and `as!`, `try!`, implicitly unwrapped optionals) neither its configuration nor a file-wide `swift-format-ignore-file` switches off, and whose own test exemption reaches only SwiftPM's test targets: `import XCTest` is refused everywhere and Swift Testing outside a test target; SwiftLint for the never-crash calls (`fatalError`, `exit`, `abort` and the like, called or taken as a value), every postfix `!`, `.unsafelyUnwrapped` and the pointer APIs confined to `Platform/` in tests too, read from Swift's own syntax tree (D-28); every target, test targets included (`build build-for-testing`), built for the iOS Simulator, with an import the package does not declare an error (`DIAGNOSE_MISSING_TARGET_DEPENDENCIES=YES_ERROR`), so `CraftBridge` cannot import a plugin |
| Android | Spotless (ktlint, from the root `.editorconfig` alone), detekt for the never-crash calls and the JNI declarations confined to `platform/` in every source set, read from Kotlin's own syntax tree (D-28), Android Lint, the release build and the unit-test and instrumented-test Kotlin compilations, with warnings as errors; the build itself refuses a module that skips the convention plugin or sets its rules back, a check the gate asks for that no longer brings the tasks doing its work, and a project dependency, declared or resolved, from `:core` on any module or from a plugin module on anything but `:core`; a task any module disables or skips with `onlyIf` reports SKIPPED, which `cargo xtask skipped-tasks` reads from Gradle's log and fails the stage on |
| Shell | `shellcheck --norc` on every script, told by its extension or its `#!` line, bar the Gradle wrapper and the plan kit's `plan/plan` |
| Duplicates | jscpd over Rust, Swift, Kotlin and shell: a block of ten lines, or of seventy tokens, repeated anywhere fails, in two passes because jscpd applies its two minimums together; generated directories and build output are skipped, and nothing else is: jscpd runs with `--no-gitignore`, and the rules refuse the `.ignore` files, nested `.gitignore` files and ignore markers it would honour |
| Conformance | the desktop corpus (§28), from QA-1 on |

Until OPS-6, OPS-7 and OPS-8 land, `cargo xtask rules` makes the Swift and Kotlin checks named in the Swift and Android rows, and reads `unsafe` and lint attributes in Rust, on text with its comments and literals stripped (OPS-3); each of those tasks moves its checks onto the language's syntax tree and out of the rules stage.

**Gate machinery.** The gate's own machinery decides what the gate checks, so it cannot guard itself: `tools/ci.sh`, `tools/env.sh`, `tools/hooks/`, `rust/xtask/`, `rust/.cargo/config.toml`, `android/sdk/settings.gradle.kts`, `android/sdk/gradle.properties`, `android/sdk/build-logic/`, and the single copy of each of `rust/clippy.toml`, `rust/rustfmt.toml`, `rust/deny.toml`, `ios/sdk/.swift-format`, `tools/licences.toml` and the root `.editorconfig`. A change to any of those files is a gate change, which its pull request names and whose review checks for weakened rules; the gate fails on a second copy of any listed configuration file, or of a tool configuration that would act like one, anywhere in the tree (AGENTS §10, decision #120): cargo-deny's `deny.exceptions.toml` and `.deny.exceptions.toml` widen `rust/deny.toml`'s allowlist, ktlint merges every `.editorconfig` up to the root's, and Cargo reads a `rust/.cargo/config` in place of `config.toml`. Tool configurations the gate keeps none of fail it wherever they sit: `.shellcheckrc` and `shellcheckrc`, which shellcheck reads as directives (it also runs with `--norc`), `.ignore` and any `.gitignore` but the root's and `plan/`'s, which jscpd honours (it also runs with `--no-gitignore`), and a jscpd ignore marker in the code folders. Gradle reads a `gradle.properties` in a project's own folder as that project's properties, so no other `gradle.properties` sits under `android/sdk`: the build's own is `android/sdk/gradle.properties` alone, and `android/sdk/build-logic`, an included build with properties of its own, is where its own may sit (AGENTS §10, decision #122).

**Module build files.** An Android module's build file applies the convention plugin and names its namespace once, and holds only comments, `plugins { id("craftbridge.android.library") }`, `android { namespace = "io.github.christopherlinnett.craftbridge.<module>" }` and a `dependencies` block whose entries are `api`, `implementation`, `testImplementation` or `androidTestImplementation` of a `project(":…")` or a `libs.<alias>`; the root `android/sdk/build.gradle.kts` holds only comments and a `plugins` block of `alias(libs.plugins.<alias>) apply false` lines and `id("craftbridge.quality")`. Every module the settings include has its build file, spelled exactly `build.gradle.kts` because a case-insensitive disk would hand Gradle a `Build.gradle.kts` all the same, no build file is written in Groovy — Gradle would read `build.gradle` in place of `build.gradle.kts`, and the rule reads only Kotlin — and anything else a build needs is configured once in `android/sdk/build-logic`, so a module's file never carries the reach to rewire a check the gate relies on (AGENTS §10, decision #121).
